gaps.lead: He lost his job because he kept arriving late.
gaps.sentence: If he hadn't kept arriving late, he ___ his job.
gaps.explanation: If + past perfect, would(n't) have + participle.

gaps.lead: The show was so dull that half the audience left.
gaps.sentence: It was ___ that half the audience left.
gaps.explanation: so dull (a show) → such a dull show.

gaps.lead: I would love to afford a bigger flat.
gaps.explanation: wish + subject + could = regret about ability/possibility.

gaps.lead: People think she was the best singer of her generation.
gaps.sentence: She ___ the best singer of her generation.
gaps.explanation: A present belief about a past event uses is thought to have + participle.

gaps.lead: I haven't seen such a good film for ages.
gaps.sentence: It was ___ I had seen for ages.
gaps.explanation: Not…such a good film for ages = the best film (I had seen) for ages.

gaps.lead: I can't wait for the holidays to begin.
gaps.explanation: look forward TO + -ing/noun: looking forward to the holidays beginning.
